author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Combine controller and touchscreen inputs
summary: Assign clear ownership between a physical controller and touch overlay, expose only missing functions, and test switching, simultaneous input, reconnect, and neutral release.
heroAlt: PCSX2 input scene representing deliberate switching between a physical controller and a small supplemental touch control set

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals

blocks.text: Assign ownership before combining input sources

Write an ownership table before binding anything: assign movement, camera, and frequent actions to the physical controller, then list only the missing functions the overlay will supply. Begin with two separately verified profiles. Add one touch action at a time while the controller stays connected, and use a scene where both sources can be exercised without loading or cutscene timing.

Avoid mapping the same PS2 control to both sources unless simultaneous ownership is intentional and tested. Duplicate bindings can emit two presses, leave an action held when one source releases, or trigger an emulator hotkey before the game receives input. Keep menu, fast-forward, and save-state controls away from touch regions used during ordinary play.

items: Physical controller passes its own complete mapping test.
Touch overlay releases cleanly when tested alone.
Short list of PS2 functions missing from the physical device.
Save separate live-input traces for the complete pad profile and complete touch profile before adding any shared action.
Choose a sequence that holds a physical stick while invoking each overlay-only function, including one pause and resume transition.

blocks.text: Add the smallest useful touch supplement

items: 1. Keep movement, camera, and primary actions owned by the controller.
2. Expose only missing buttons or occasional commands on the touch overlay.
3. Inspect shared PS2 functions for duplicate physical and touch bindings.
4. Press a controller direction, tap the supplemental control, and release in reverse order.
5. Switch between sources repeatedly while watching neutral state.
6. Background and resume the app with the controller still connected.
7. Reconnect the controller and verify touch remains available without taking Port 1.
8. Save the hybrid arrangement with its exact device and purpose in the name.

blocks.text: Watch the live input display while alternating sources. A controller press should create one transition and return to neutral before the corresponding touch test begins. Then hold a stick on the pad while tapping the overlay action. A failure only during the combined step identifies merge or multi-input state, not a bad standalone controller or touch mapping.

Complete a short gameplay route using the intended handoff: navigate with the pad, invoke each overlay-only function, hold one controller direction during a touch press, pause, resume, and repeat. Disconnect and reconnect the pad; the overlay must remain usable and controller events must not duplicate when the device returns.

items: One action produces one PS2 transition regardless of source.
Simultaneous controller and touch values coexist where the game requires them.
Disconnecting the pad does not leave an axis or button held.
The final ownership table must account for every PS2 control and show that no action emits duplicate press or release transitions.
Reconnect the pad during a cold-launched session; touch-only functions must remain available and controller events must return once.
Menus advance twice: remove one duplicate binding for that PS2 function.
The overlay disappears after pad input: inspect the app's input-mode visibility setting.
Touch steals player assignment: keep both sources feeding the intended port only.
Resume leaves movement active: release all input and reproduce lifecycle handling.

blocks.text: Separate the two input profiles again

Disable the hybrid profile and reload the two known-good standalone profiles. Remove only bindings added for cross-source use, then inspect the live display for a fully neutral state. If a control stays held, restart the input session before continuing; do not compensate with a larger dead zone or unrelated game timing changes.
Not every game accepts rapid source changes gracefully

Hybrid input depends on explicit ownership. Android may reorder devices after reconnect, while touch contacts can be cancelled by system gestures or app lifecycle changes. Document which source owns every nonstandard action and retest after input-backend updates. If the game itself rejects simultaneous opposite commands, preserve that limitation rather than masking it with more mappings.
